characters: A hen, a duck, a goat, a dog, a cat, a cow, a rooster, a bee and a frog around a village compound, drawn kindly and safely, with a child watching from the veranda.

narrationPlan.voice: Playful voice; each animal sound is made with its own voice
narrationPlan.pace: Playful, with a pause so children can make the sounds (about 70 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: A sing-song tune with a pause after each animal for children to answer (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Farm and compound animals are familiar to many Ghanaian children. Animal sounds are written differently in different languages; teachers can add the sounds children use at home.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Check that the animal sounds are right for Ghanaian English and that the page does not suggest children should touch unfamiliar animals.

pages.narration: Buzz softly, tweet lightly, croak low.

teacherGuide.overview: A call-and-answer rhyme for animal sounds. Form: four couplets. Rhyming pairs: quack/back, mew/do, day/play, tweet/feet. Sound words help phonics and speaking.
learningGoals: Take turns in a call-and-answer game.
beforeReading: Show pictures of the animals. Ask children what sound each makes.
whileReading: Pause before each sound so children answer. Do not rush.
afterReading: Play a guessing game: make a sound and let children name the animal.
Add a new couplet for a sheep or a donkey.
discussion: Which animals live at your home or near it?
How should we behave around animals?
reflection: How can we be kind to animals?

support: Use pictures and let children point to the animal.
stretch: Invent a funny animal and say what sound it makes.

culturalNotes: Farm and compound animals are familiar to many Ghanaian children. Animal sounds are written differently in different languages; teachers can add the sounds children use at home.
localiseThis: Add the animal sounds children know in their home language.
Teach safety: never touch a strange animal, and wash your hands after touching any animal.
